column3: False positive: the name sits in t.mock.timers.enable({ apis: [setTimeout] }), which installs fake time; the budget timers of withBudget are fired by t.mock.timers.tick, nothing waits for a duration

False positive: the name sits in t.mock.timers.enable({ apis: [setTimeout] }), which installs fake time; the hook budget timer is fired by t.mock.timers.tick once the worker is inside its command, nothing waits

False positive: heldClock replaces globalThis.setTimeout by a clock that only stores the limit and grace callbacks; the test fires them when the event they are about is true, nothing waits for a duration
False positive: every setTimeout in this file is text the test feeds to the scanner as a fixture, or a pattern it asserts on in the scanner output or in a finding; no wait is run

Real 20 ms poll between checks of state a separate process writes (the shell-script fake runtimes of dispatch-lib.mjs: pid files, markers, ledger lines, a process that has ended); the fakes cannot tell the test. To remove it the fakes report over a socket (event-lib.mjs) and a process gone becomes the close of its connection. Used only by dispatch.test.mjs and dispatch-watchdog.test.mjs; the run-time failsafe is the only duration
